lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hi Linda, it's Pierre from the coaching program. Is now still a good time?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Not bad. Sleeping better.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Oh, and I've had a fever since last night. 101. I'm still on chemo.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Thank you for telling me. That's something your care team needs to hear today. I'm going to call the nurse line as soon as we hang up, and if it gets worse, please go to the ER or call 911.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes, that's fine.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Tell me how the drinks on the weekend went this week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I did it 1 days, then the weekend happened.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the drinks on the weekend going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Once you decide something, you follow through.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm going to do it Monday, Wednesday and Friday.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why is this important to you right now?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll set an alarm on my phone. At least I'm trying.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What did you notice on the days it went well?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I want to get my energy back.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want to feel like yourself again.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'd like to be able to keep up with my grandkids.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You want your energy back.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It was a long weekend with family, you know how it is.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Do you drink mostly on weekends?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. Okay, this week I'll really do it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is it mostly beer?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sometimes.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before. I feel guilty when I skip it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Would it be okay if I shared something that's helped other people?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Go ahead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Having a glass of water between drinks is an easy way to slow down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I've tried this before and it never lasts.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Is that something you can do?

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I think so.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I put a reminder on the fridge. My doctor said the same thing.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Can I share an idea?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Having a glass of water between drinks is an easy way to slow down.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I feel so much better on Sunday when I don't overdo it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You're starting to see that small changes add up.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already told my family about my goal.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How would things be different if you kept this up?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yeah, I like what I eat. I'm not going to change at my age.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let's put you down to keep it to 3 drinks on the weekend next week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know, I know.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: On a scale of 0 to 10, how confident are you that you can do that?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Like a 8.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Why a 8 and not a 5?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I can stick to two beers if I eat first.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What might get in the way?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll go to the mall instead.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So, to sum up: the parties made this week harder, you still got 1 days in, and your plan is to keep it to 3 drinks on the weekend. Sound right?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Yes. You got it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Same time next Monday?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That works.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Linda, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, Pierre. Bye!

flags.reason: Participant reports 101 F fever while on chemo. Coach escalated to nurse line, but supervisor should confirm the nurse call happened today and that she was given clear ER/911 criteria before the call ended.
'Once you decide something, you follow through' lectures the participant without permission, right after she expressed uncertainty about following through.
Water-between-drinks tip given after permission, then met with 'never lasts' (sustain talk). Coach moved on, then repeated the same tip at line 39 without exploring the resistance.
'Let's put you down to keep it to 3 drinks' sets a goal unilaterally right after sustain talk ('not going to change at my age'). Goal was not collaboratively negotiated.

score.summary: Linda reported a fever on chemotherapy and Pierre appropriately committed to same-day nurse escalation and ER guidance. The alcohol coaching was strong on open questions and change talk, but it was undermined by persuading, repeating an unwanted tip, and imposing a 3-drink goal.
strengths: Line 6: Took the fever report seriously and arranged same-day nurse escalation with clear ER/911 instructions.
Line 26 and 49: Used open questions to draw out her own reasons and confidence ratings.
Line 53: Ended with a clear summary and confirmed next contact at line 55.
coaching_tips: Line 45: Replace the imposed 3-drink goal with a collaborative question, e.g., 'What limit feels doable to you for next weekend?'
Line 12 and 39: Avoid lecturing or repeating a tip she already rejected; ask permission first and explore her 'it never lasts' concern.
Line 33: Use a reflection on her doubt (e.g., 'Past attempts have been hard') instead of 'I see' before moving on.
Line 6: Confirm the nurse call is completed today and check whether she is able to get help if symptoms worsen.
